title: Filleted L-bracket under a side load: the peak von Mises stress on the R6 fillet, coarse tet10 mesh
source: mesh convergence of the finite element solution (P. J. Roache, Verification and Validation in Computational Science and Engineering, Hermosa, 1998, ch. 5): the bracket has no closed-form stress; the reference is the mesh-independent peak of a four-level study of quadratic tetrahedral meshes refined by √2 in size and in curvature resolution (README.md); equilibrium

quantities.quantity: largest nodal von Mises stress on the fillet face (MPa)
quantities.reason: at this level (16 mm, one element per 90° of the fillet) the peak moves with the mesh by more than at the finer ones: 213.3 MPa (macOS) and 210.2 MPa (Linux) for the kernel's face order before the mesher took its input in a canonical order, 203.6 MPa after (#115), so the band is 5%; the four-level study gives 213.3, 210.6, 214.3, 213.3 MPa (2k to 13.5k elements): the bending stress is converged across the fillet, and the peak nodal value moves only with which of the fillet's tessellation lines (fixed angles, through every level) carries the largest node, by under 2%
quantities.fixture_reason: the peak depends on the tet mesh, which is generated from SolidCraft's tessellation of the bracket; that tessellation is not bit-identical across platforms (its coordinates differ in the last bits between arm64 and x86-64 builds, issue #115). The tet mesher itself gives the same mesh for the same tessellation on every platform, run and thread count (fieldcraft-mesh `the_quality_mesh_is_the_same_on_every_platform`, testkit `tet_meshes_do_not_depend_on_the_run_or_the_thread_count`), so the quantity can be frozen once the tessellation is reproducible; until then the reference tolerance gates it
